question: Can sparse-autoencoder selection be framed as lossy minimum-description-length coding so that dictionary width, activation sparsity, precision, and reconstruction quality trade off more principledly than an L0 proxy for interpretability?

key_findings.claim: The paper gives a useful rate-distortion interpretation of an SAE: communicate a shared decoder plus quantized sparse latent activations under a reconstruction or downstream-loss tolerance.
key_findings.evidence: It defines epsilon-MDL optimality as the shortest description among SAEs whose reconstruction loss is below epsilon and estimates activation cost from quantized per-feature entropies. For a simple upper bound, an L0-sparse code over D features with B-bit nonzero values costs approximately L0(B+log2 D), exposing a width-sparsity trade-off hidden by L0 alone.

anchors.section: 4 SAEs should be sparse, but not too sparse, Equation 1

key_findings.claim: Under the paper's simplified activation-only code, both dense/narrow and one-hot/wide extremes are longer than a representative GPT-2 SAE, illustrating why maximal sparsity is not identical to maximal compression.
key_findings.evidence: Using seven bits per positive activation, the paper estimates 1,405 bits/token for a 25,000-feature GPT-2 SAE with L0=65, versus 5,376 bits for 768 dense activations and 13,993 bits for a one-hot dictionary indexed over vocabulary-position combinations. The comparison is explicitly approximate because the SAE is lossy while the extremes are lossless.

key_findings.claim: On raw MNIST pixels at fixed MSE, the minimum estimated latent description occurs at an intermediate width/sparsity whose decoder atoms look like reusable strokes rather than tiny fragments or memorized digits.
key_findings.evidence: BatchTopK SAEs are trained to test MSE about 0.0150 over a hyperparameter sweep. Dense/narrow models yield small local or PCA-like features, very sparse/wide models yield whole-digit exemplars, and the visualized MDL minimum yields longer line segments. No blinded human rating, semantic metric, seed stability analysis, or LLM-activation experiment is reported.

anchors.section: 5 MDL-SAEs find interpretable and composable features for MNIST, Figure 3

key_findings.claim: A toy Boolean analysis shows that minimizing L0 always rewards splitting a co-occurring conjunction into its own mutually exclusive feature, whereas entropy coding only rewards the split when correlation makes it cheaper.
key_findings.evidence: Without splitting, L0=pA+pB and description length is H(pA)+H(pB); adding an A-and-B feature reduces L0 by p(A and B), but its three mutually exclusive codes are shorter only in part of the correlation-probability phase diagram. This is a conceptual criterion, not an empirical demonstration that MDL suppresses feature splitting in language-model SAEs.

anchors.section: 6 Optimising for MDL can reduce undesirable feature splitting, Figure 4

key_findings.claim: The proposed 'independent additivity' and hierarchy ideas are promising design constraints, but the paper overstates them as sufficient or necessary for interpretability.
key_findings.evidence: A linear decoder makes reconstructed activation vectors additive, and a parent-child code can replace marginal entropy with conditional entropy. Yet linear reconstruction does not make downstream causal effects additive through a nonlinear language model, semantic explanations can depend on interactions, and additive explanations do not imply statistically independent feature activations.

anchors.section: 7 Hierarchical features allow more efficient coding

method.core_idea: Select an SAE as a two-part lossy code, minimizing bits needed for its feature activations and decoder subject to a chosen fidelity tolerance, while constraining explanations to decompose additively or hierarchically.
method.mechanism: Train a grid of BatchTopK SAEs at matched reconstruction error, quantize nonzero latent values until the error budget is reached, estimate entropy per feature, and choose the lowest-description model. Boolean examples compare split versus compositional codes and flat versus conditional hierarchical codes.
assumptions: Shorter activation codes at fixed fidelity correlate with human-understandable explanations.
Decoder cost is asymptotically negligible relative to activation cost for the intended dataset size and can be omitted in the demonstrated selection calculation.
Per-feature marginal entropies are an appropriate code length despite dependencies among activations.
Feature explanations should compose independently and additively for humans to understand them.
MSE on MNIST pixels is a meaningful proxy for the faithfulness constraint relevant to neural activations.
Quantization and entropy estimates generalize from the finite sample used to select the model.

techniques.role: Chooses the shortest SAE code among models satisfying a reconstruction or downstream-loss tolerance.
Estimates communication cost from discretized nonzero feature activations.
Charges both for active values and the indices needed to address a wider dictionary.
Derives when an explicit conjunction reduces entropy rather than merely L0.
Encodes a child feature only when its parent is active to exploit semantic hierarchy.
Provides the sole empirical case study at matched pixel reconstruction error.

evaluations.setting: Illustrative GPT-2 residual-stream code-length arithmetic using a published 25,000-feature SAE, dense activations, and a token-position one-hot extreme.
evaluations.result: 1,405 bits for the SAE versus 5,376 dense and 13,993 one-hot under the stated precision assumptions.
evaluations.baseline: Lossless dense activations and an exemplar-like one-hot dictionary.

evaluations.setting: BatchTopK SAEs trained for 1,000+ epochs on MNIST over width/L0 hyperparameters at test MSE 0.0150, with roughly five-bit nonzero quantization.
evaluations.metric: Estimated latent description length and qualitative decoder-feature appearance.
evaluations.result: An intermediate width/sparsity minimizes estimated bits and visually yields stroke-like atoms.

evaluations.setting: Analytic two-Boolean toy distributions with and without an explicit conjunction feature.
evaluations.metric: Expected L0 and entropy-derived description length.
evaluations.result: Splitting always lowers L0 but lowers description length only above a probability/correlation-dependent boundary.
evaluations.baseline: Compositional reconstruction of the conjunction from two additive features.

evaluations.setting: Analytic parent-child concept pair such as Animal and Bird.
evaluations.result: The hierarchical conditional code is always shorter in the proposed setup even though it has higher expected L0.
evaluations.baseline: Two mutually exclusive flat SAE features.

limitations: The only trained demonstration uses raw MNIST images, not activations of a language model, and interpretability is judged qualitatively by the authors.
No causal, downstream-task, feature-label, human-rating, or automated-interpretability metric validates that the MDL-selected features explain model computation better.
The demonstrated description length omits the width-dependent decoder, entropy-model, codebook, and architecture costs required by a strict finite-sample two-part MDL code.
Summing marginal feature entropies overpays when features are dependent; independent semantic additivity does not entail probabilistic independence.
Linear decoder additivity does not guarantee additive interventions or causal effects after the reconstructed activation passes through nonlinear downstream layers.
The fidelity threshold and distortion metric are user choices that can change the selected model, and selecting on test MSE risks test-set tuning.
MDL is used only after an expensive sweep, not optimized end-to-end, and no comparison of compute or selection stability is provided.
failure_modes: A compact cryptic code compresses well but has no stable human semantic interpretation.
An omitted large decoder makes a wide memorization dictionary appear artificially cheap.
Correlated activations cause the marginal-entropy score to rank models differently from an actual joint compressor.
A model preserves pixel MSE or activation variance while deleting low-variance features crucial to downstream behavior.
A semantically meaningful interaction is rejected because it violates the paper's additive explanation constraint.
Finite-sample entropy estimates favor rare or dead features and do not transfer to a changed activation distribution.
reusable_insights: SAE width should carry an explicit addressing cost; L0 alone makes ever-wider dictionaries look misleadingly attractive.
Interpretability selection should be formulated at fixed faithfulness, ideally using downstream loss rather than only activation MSE.
Feature splitting can be evaluated as a coding decision: introduce a conjunction only when its repeated use saves more bits than its extra identity cost.
Hierarchical or conditional codes offer a principled way to represent multiple semantic granularities without forcing them into mutually exclusive flat atoms.
A serious MDL benchmark should publish an executable codec, include model costs, and compare its bits with causal and human-centered utility metrics.
open_questions: Does strict finite-sample MDL select better LLM SAEs under blinded human, causal intervention, and practical downstream evaluations?
What joint or structured entropy model captures SAE dependencies while remaining human-readable?
Can decoder and codebook costs be amortized honestly across a stated activation corpus and deployment horizon?
Can a differentiable rate-distortion objective train the selected architecture directly instead of requiring a large sweep?
When are nonlinear feature interactions themselves the simplest faithful explanation, and how should they be coded?
How stable is the MDL optimum across data domains, seeds, activation layers, quantizers, and fidelity thresholds?

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Immediate large-scale SAE study establishing reconstruction-sparsity scaling laws and metrics that generally improve with dictionary size.
competitive_landscape.difference: Gao et al. train up to 16 million GPT-4 latents and evaluate hypothesized-feature recovery, explainability, and downstream-effect sparsity; the target argues that adding an addressing-rate cost can reverse the pressure toward ever-wider dictionaries but tests only MNIST.

competitive_landscape.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current standardized alternative to a single compression proxy, measuring seven axes over more than 200 SAEs and eight methods.
competitive_landscape.difference: SAEBench finds unsupervised proxy gains do not reliably transfer to disentanglement, unlearning, or other applications; MDL-SAE proposes a principled scalar selection objective but provides no evidence yet that its optimum transfers.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct empirical investigation of width-dependent feature splitting, incompleteness, and non-atomicity using SAE stitching and meta-SAEs.
competitive_landscape.difference: Leask et al. show empirically that larger dictionaries contain novel and decomposable features and recommend task-dependent granularity; the target derives an entropy criterion intended to select granularity before demonstrating it on LLMs.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Subsequent direct architectural realization of hierarchical multi-granularity SAEs, a direction proposed conceptually by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: Matryoshka SAEs train nested dictionaries jointly and improve probing, concept erasure, disentanglement, and feature absorption on Gemma-2-2B/TinyStories; the target supplies a coding rationale and conditional-tree proposal but no hierarchical implementation.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Core empirical SAE baseline demonstrating interpretable features in small language models and motivating sparsity as a practical decomposition approach.
competitive_landscape.difference: Cunningham et al. validate actual language-model features with automated and qualitative evidence; the target focuses on information-theoretic model selection and does not test whether MDL improves those evaluations.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current meta-evaluation showing that even multi-metric SAE benchmarks can have high reseed noise, low discriminability, and weak synthetic-ground-truth validity.
competitive_landscape.difference: Chanin audits measurement reliability directly; the target offers an objective coding score whose reliability, sensitivity, and correlation with ground truth still require the same style of audit.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after checking large-scale SAE scaling, canonical-unit critiques, Matryoshka SAEs, SAEBench, and its current audit: MDL and rate-distortion are established in sparse coding, but explicitly charging SAE feature-addressing cost and deriving splitting/hierarchy examples is a valuable conceptual contribution for mechanistic interpretability. Subsequent Matryoshka work makes the hierarchy direction concrete. The paper should currently be treated as a model-selection hypothesis, not evidence that compression operationalizes human or causal interpretability in LLMs.
reviewer_notes: Read all 11 extracted pages, including the MNIST procedure and coding examples. The review distinguishes decoder-vector additivity, semantic explanation additivity, statistical independence, and downstream causal additivity, which the paper sometimes moves between too quickly. Competitor records were checked against primary arXiv and OpenReview pages on 2026-08-23.
